s1.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and hemorrhagic stroke
salient_findings: Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
key_facts: Hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
Hypertension again at age 38 after basal ganglia hemorrhage
Splenomegaly diagnosed at age 21
Younger brother with similar splenomegaly finding
Normochromic microcytic anemia and thrombocytopenia on full blood examination
Low HDL and elevated triglycerides on lipid profile
Bilateral adrenal lesions on renal Doppler ultrasound and CT
Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins on CT
No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess
Blood pressure controlled on a single antihypertensive agent

differentials: Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Cancer
per_call: Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Cancer

shortlist.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar splenomegaly finding and presence of basal ganglia hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Primary Myelofibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly, anemia, and thrombocytopenia are consistent with myeloproliferative neoplasm

shortlist.label: Systemic Mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly and presence of anemia and thrombocytopenia could be related to mast cell proliferation

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis Nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension, renal involvement, and presence of anemia and thrombocytopenia are consistent with vasculitis

shortlist.label: Hereditary Spherocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar splenomegaly finding and presence of normochromic microcytic anemia

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with splenomegaly at a young age, normochromic microcytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins is consistent with Primary Myelofibrosis, a myeloproliferative neoplasm that can lead to portal hypertension and associated complications.

rejected.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
rejected.why: While it could explain the basal ganglia hemorrhage, it doesn't account for the hematologic abnormalities and hepatosplenomegaly.

rejected.label: Systemic Mastocytosis
rejected.why: There's no mention of mast cell mediator-related symptoms or findings suggestive of mastocytosis.

rejected.label: Polyarteritis Nodosa
rejected.why: The patient lacks systemic vasculitis symptoms and the findings are more suggestive of a myeloproliferative disorder.

rejected.label: Hereditary Spherocytosis
rejected.why: The patient's anemia is described as normochromic microcytic, not consistent with the normochromic anemia typically seen in hereditary spherocytosis.
